/-! ## Edge-count profile -/

/-- The **edge-count profile** of a finite (pseudo)metric space: the number of edges of
    the Rips graph at integer threshold `r`. We use `Set.ncard` so no decidability
    instance is required; finiteness is automatic from `Fintype α`. -/
def ripsEdgeCount (α : Type*) [PseudoMetricSpace α] [Fintype α] (r : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (ripsGraph α (r : ℝ)).edgeSet.ncard

/-- The edge set of a Rips graph over a finite type is finite. -/
theorem ripsEdgeSet_finite (α : Type*) [PseudoMetricSpace α] [Fintype α] (r : ℕ) :
    (ripsGraph α (r : ℝ)).edgeSet.Finite :=
  Set.toFinite _

/-- **Monotonicity of the edge-count profile.** Larger threshold ⇒ at least as many edges.
    This is the cardinality-functor image of `ripsGraph_mono`. -/
theorem ripsEdgeCount_mono (α : Type*) [PseudoMetricSpace α] [Fintype α] :
    Monotone (ripsEdgeCount α) := by
  intro a b h
  refine Set.ncard_le_ncard ?_ (ripsEdgeSet_finite α b)
  exact SimpleGraph.edgeSet_subset_edgeSet.mpr (ripsGraph_mono (by exact_mod_cast h))

/-- **Normalization at the bottom threshold.** In a metric space the Rips graph at
    threshold `0` is empty, so the profile starts at `0`. Uses `ripsGraph_bot_of_metric`. -/
theorem ripsEdgeCount_bot (α : Type*) [MetricSpace α] [Fintype α] :
    ripsEdgeCount α 0 = 0 := by
  unfold ripsEdgeCount
  rw [Nat.cast_zero, ripsGraph_bot_of_metric, SimpleGraph.edgeSet_bot, Set.ncard_empty]

    the standard tropical object on `ℕ`, into which the edge-count profile lands. -/
def ripsTropObj (_α : Type*) : TropObj := ⟨ℕ, tropicalization_base⟩

/-- The edge-count profile is **normalized** at the tropical zero. -/
theorem ripsProfile_normalized (α : Type*) [MetricSpace α] [Fintype α] :
    ripsEdgeCount α 0 = tropicalization_base.zero :=
  ripsEdgeCount_bot α

/-- The edge-count profile is **monotone in the tropical order** `tropicalization_base.le`. -/
theorem ripsProfile_trop_mono (α : Type*) [PseudoMetricSpace α] [Fintype α]
    {r₁ r₂ : ℕ} (h : r₁ ≤ r₂) :
    tropicalization_base.le (ripsEdgeCount α r₁) (ripsEdgeCount α r₂) :=
  ripsEdgeCount_mono α h

    (`= max`) of two profile values at comparable thresholds equals the larger one.
    This couples `ripsEdgeCount_mono` with `tropicalization_base.max_op`. -/
theorem ripsProfile_max_chain (α : Type*) [PseudoMetricSpace α] [Fintype α]
    {r₁ r₂ : ℕ} (h : r₁ ≤ r₂) :
    tropicalization_base.max_op (ripsEdgeCount α r₁) (ripsEdgeCount α r₂)
      = ripsEdgeCount α r₂ := by
  show max (ripsEdgeCount α r₁) (ripsEdgeCount α r₂) = ripsEdgeCount α r₂
  exact max_eq_right (ripsEdgeCount_mono α h)

theorem ripsProfile_add_chain (α : Type*) [PseudoMetricSpace α] [Fintype α]
    {r₁ r₂ : ℕ} (h : r₁ ≤ r₂) :
    tropicalization_base.add (ripsEdgeCount α r₁) (ripsEdgeCount α r₂)

  show max (ripsEdgeCount α r₁) (ripsEdgeCount α r₂) = ripsEdgeCount α r₂

import Mathlib
import Bridges.RipsTropical.Core

open CategoricalTropicalUltrametric

noncomputable section

namespace RipsTropical

/-- A map `f` is **nonexpanding** (1-Lipschitz) if it does not increase distances. -/
def Nonexpanding {α β : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace α] [PseudoMetricSpace β]
    (f : α → β) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y, dist (f x) (f y) ≤ dist x y

/-- **Main functoriality estimate.** An injective nonexpanding map of finite metric
    spaces induces a pointwise inequality of edge-count profiles: each edge of the
    source Rips graph maps injectively to an edge of the target Rips graph. -/
theorem nonexpansive_injective_edgeCount_le
    {α β : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace α] [PseudoMetricSpace β] [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    (f : α → β) (hf_inj : Function.Injective f) (hf_ne : Nonexpanding f) (r : ℕ) :
    ripsEdgeCount α r ≤ ripsEdgeCount β r := by
  refine Set.ncard_le_ncard_of_injOn (Sym2.map f) ?_ ?_ (ripsEdgeSet_finite β r)
  · intro e he
    induction e using Sym2.ind with
    | _ x y =>
      rw [SimpleGraph.mem_edgeSet] at he
      obtain ⟨hne, hd⟩ := he
      rw [Sym2.map_pair_eq, SimpleGraph.mem_edgeSet]
      refine ⟨fun hfxy => hne (hf_inj hfxy), ?_⟩
      exact le_trans (hf_ne x y) hd
  · exact (Sym2.map.injective hf_inj).injOn

/-- The same estimate, stated through the tropical order `tropicalization_base.le`,
    exhibiting it as a **monotone morphism** of the induced valuation data. -/
theorem nonexpansive_injective_trop_dom
    {α β : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace α] [PseudoMetricSpace β] [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    (f : α → β) (hf_inj : Function.Injective f) (hf_ne : Nonexpanding f) (r : ℕ) :
    tropicalization_base.le (ripsEdgeCount α r) (ripsEdgeCount β r) :=
  nonexpansive_injective_edgeCount_le f hf_inj hf_ne r

/-- **Domination of profiles.** The source profile is tropically dominated by the target
    profile at every threshold. This is the morphism relation in the thin category of
    finite metric spaces mapped into `tropicalization_base`. -/
def RipsProfileDomination (α β : Type*)
    [PseudoMetricSpace α] [PseudoMetricSpace β] [Fintype α] [Fintype β] : Prop :=
  ∀ r : ℕ, tropicalization_base.le (ripsEdgeCount α r) (ripsEdgeCount β r)

/-- An injective nonexpanding map yields a domination of profiles. -/
theorem dom_of_nonexpansive_injective
    {α β : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace α] [PseudoMetricSpace β] [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    (f : α → β) (hf_inj : Function.Injective f) (hf_ne : Nonexpanding f) :
    RipsProfileDomination α β :=
  fun r => nonexpansive_injective_trop_dom f hf_inj hf_ne r

/-- Reflexivity: the identity is injective and nonexpanding, so every profile dominates
    itself. -/
theorem dom_refl (α : Type*) [PseudoMetricSpace α] [Fintype α] :
    RipsProfileDomination α α :=
  fun r => tropicalization_base.le_refl (ripsEdgeCount α r)

/-- Transitivity: domination composes (functoriality of the bridge under composition). -/
theorem dom_trans {α β γ : Type*}
    [PseudoMetricSpace α] [PseudoMetricSpace β] [PseudoMetricSpace γ]
    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype γ]
    (hαβ : RipsProfileDomination α β) (hβγ : RipsProfileDomination β γ) :
    RipsProfileDomination α γ :=
  fun r => tropicalization_base.le_trans (hαβ r) (hβγ r)

/-- Composition of injective nonexpanding maps is injective nonexpanding, so the induced
    domination relation is closed under composition — the functor respects composition. -/
theorem nonexpanding_comp {α β γ : Type*}
    [PseudoMetricSpace α] [PseudoMetricSpace β] [PseudoMetricSpace γ]
    {g : β → γ} {f : α → β} (hg : Nonexpanding g) (hf : Nonexpanding f) :
    Nonexpanding (g ∘ f) := by
  intro x y
  exact le_trans (hg (f x) (f y)) (hf x y)

end RipsTropical

/-
  # A 1-Lipschitz Functor from Valuation-Depth Measures to Tropical Valuation Objects

  Bridge: connects `Computation/PadicValuationDepth` (valuation-depth complexity measures)
  to `Bridges/CategoricalTropicalUltrametric` (tropical valuation objects).

  **Core principle.** A valuation-depth measure assigns to each function a depth `vdepth`
  satisfying the *non-Archimedean composition laws*

      vdepth (f + g) ≤ max (vdepth f) (vdepth g) + 1
      vdepth (f * g) ≤ max (vdepth f) (vdepth g) + 1

  This is *exactly* the statement that `vdepth`, viewed as a map into the tropical
  valuation object `(ℕ, max, ·)`, is **1-Lipschitz with respect to the tropical
  addition (= max), up to a unit cost**.  The "+1" is the Lipschitz constant of the
  bridge: combining two depth-bounded objects costs at most one extra unit of depth.

  We package the depth data into a bundled object `DepthCarrier`, exhibit the functor
  `depthTropObj` into the catalog's `TropObj`, prove the central 1-Lipschitz laws, and
  then develop the *deep content*: the logarithmic-overhead theorem.  A balanced binary
  combination tree of `2^n` depth-`d` leaves evaluates to depth `≤ d + n = d + log₂(2^n)`.
  This bridges the unit-cost 1-Lipschitz law to the `O(log n)` Hensel complexity theme of
  the source file (`HenselIterationComplexity`, `speedup_ratio`).

  The category of depth carriers with **nonexpansive (1-Lipschitz) morphisms** maps
  functorially to the tropical category, completing the "1-Lipschitz functor" of the title.

  -- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
  HYPOTHESIS (H0): the `vdepth_add`/`vdepth_mul` axioms of `ValuationDepthMeasure`
  are precisely a "1-Lipschitz with unit cost" condition for a map into the tropical
  semiring (ℕ, max).  CONFIRMED — the laws are reproduced verbatim as `depth_one_lipschitz_*`.

  HYPOTHESIS (H1): depth is NOT a strict tropical valuation / ultrametric seminorm
  (which would require `≤ max` with NO `+1`).  The `+1` slack is irreducible: summing a
  function with itself strictly increases depth in general.  CONFIRMED by `not_strict_ultrametric_witness`
  (we exhibit a carrier where `depth(add x x) = depth x + 1 > depth x`).  This is the
  whole novelty: the functor lands in a *1-Lipschitz relaxation* of the tropical world,
  not the strict (idempotent) tropical world of `valuationReconstruct`.

  HYPOTHESIS (H2): the unit-cost slack accumulates only logarithmically under balanced
  combination.  CONFIRMED by `depth_balanced_eval_le` (depth ≤ d + n for 2^n leaves) and
  `depth_balanced_eval_le_log` (overhead = log₂ of the number of leaves).
  This is the bridge to the `O(log n)` Hensel story.

  HYPOTHESIS (H3): the log₂ overhead is TIGHT, not just an upper bound.  CONFIRMED by
  `depth_balanced_overhead_tight`: for `witnessCarrier` the balanced tree of `2^n` leaves
  has depth EXACTLY `depth a + n`.  So the structural-height growth rate is the genuine
  cost, and a strict (slack-free) ultrametric factorization is impossible (`H1`).

  FAILURE ANALYSIS: the naive attempt to land the functor in a STRICT tropical valuation
  object (`≤ max`, `valuationReconstruct`) fails (`not_strict_ultrametric_witness`).  The
  obstruction is exactly the non-idempotency of the unit-cost addition `a ⊞ b = max a b + 1`
  (`a ⊞ a = a + 1 ≠ a`), which is why the target must be the relaxed 1-Lipschitz tropical
  object rather than the idempotent one.  ENGINEERING NOTE: stating the 1-Lipschitz laws
  through `(depthTropObj X).trop.add` directly triggered an `HAdd α ℕ` synthesis failure
  because the bundled carrier type `α` does not reduce to `ℕ` during instance search; we
  resolved this by proving `depthTropObj_trop_add : trop.add a b = max a b` and phrasing
  the laws with `max`, recovering the tropical reading definitionally.
-/

import Mathlib
import Computation.PadicValuationDepth
import Bridges.CategoricalTropicalUltrametric

namespace ValuationDepthTropicalFunctor

open CategoricalTropicalUltrametric

universe u

/-! ## §1. Depth Carriers — bundled valuation-depth measures

A `DepthCarrier` is the object-level abstraction of a `ValuationDepthMeasure`: a type with
binary operations `add`, `mul`, a `zero`, and a depth function obeying the unit-cost
non-Archimedean laws.  It is the *source object* of our functor. -/

/-- A bundled valuation-depth measure: the source object of the 1-Lipschitz functor.
    Bridge: abstracts `ValuationDepthMeasure` to an object that can be transported. -/
structure DepthCarrier where
  K : Type u
  add : K → K → K
  mul : K → K → K
  zero : K
  depth : K → ℕ
  depth_zero : depth zero = 0
  depth_add : ∀ x y, depth (add x y) ≤ max (depth x) (depth y) + 1
  depth_mul : ∀ x y, depth (mul x y) ≤ max (depth x) (depth y) + 1

/-- Build a `DepthCarrier` from any `ValuationDepthMeasure α β`: the carrier is the
    pointwise-semiring of functions `α → β` with `vdepth` as depth.
    Bridge: instantiates the abstract object from the catalog typeclass. -/
def ofValuationDepthMeasure (α β : Type*) [Semiring α] [Semiring β]
    [ValuationDepthMeasure α β] : DepthCarrier where
  K := α → β
  add := fun f g => fun x => f x + g x
  mul := fun f g => fun x => f x * g x
  zero := fun _ => 0
  depth := ValuationDepthMeasure.vdepth
  depth_zero := ValuationDepthMeasure.vdepth_zero
  depth_add := ValuationDepthMeasure.vdepth_add
  depth_mul := ValuationDepthMeasure.vdepth_mul

/-! ## §2. The Tropical Target and the Functor on Objects

The target is the catalog's standard tropical valuation object `(ℕ, max, ·)`
(`tropicalization_base`), bundled as a `TropObj`.  The functor sends every depth carrier
to this object — the depth-*value* space — exactly as the catalog's `tropicalization`
forgets ring structure and retains the norm-value semiring. -/

/-- The functor on objects: every depth carrier maps to the tropical valuation object
    `(ℕ, max, ·)`, its depth-value space. -/
def depthTropObj (_X : DepthCarrier) : TropObj := ⟨ℕ, tropicalization_base⟩

@[simp] theorem depthTropObj_alpha (X : DepthCarrier) : (depthTropObj X).α = ℕ := rfl

/-! ## §3. The Central 1-Lipschitz Laws

`depth`, viewed as a map into the tropical object `(ℕ, max)`, is 1-Lipschitz with unit
cost: combining two elements increases depth by at most the tropical-addition of their
depths plus one.  These restate the carrier axioms *through the tropical structure*. -/

/-- The target's tropical addition is literally `max` on depth values. This makes the
    1-Lipschitz statements below *tropical* statements, not merely numeric ones. -/
theorem depthTropObj_trop_add (X : DepthCarrier) (a b : ℕ) :
    (depthTropObj X).trop.add a b = max a b := rfl

/-- **1-Lipschitz (additive).** `depth (x ⊕ y) ≤ (depth x ⊞_trop depth y) + 1`, where
    `⊞_trop = max` is tropical addition in the target object (`depthTropObj_trop_add`).
    The constant `+1` is the unit Lipschitz cost of the bridge. -/
theorem depth_one_lipschitz_add (X : DepthCarrier) (x y : X.K) :
    X.depth (X.add x y) ≤ max (X.depth x) (X.depth y) + 1 :=
  X.depth_add x y

/-- **1-Lipschitz (multiplicative).** The same unit-cost bound for the product. -/
theorem depth_one_lipschitz_mul (X : DepthCarrier) (x y : X.K) :
    X.depth (X.mul x y) ≤ max (X.depth x) (X.depth y) + 1 :=
  X.depth_mul x y

/-- The depth of `zero` is the tropical zero. -/
theorem depth_zero_eq (X : DepthCarrier) :
    X.depth X.zero = (depthTropObj X).trop.zero := by
  simpa [depthTropObj, tropicalization_base] using X.depth_zero

/-! ## §4. Combination Trees — the logarithmic-overhead theorem

The unit cost compounds along the *shape* of a computation, not its size.  We model a
combination as a binary `OpTree`; the depth of the evaluated tree is bounded by the
maximum leaf depth plus the tree's height. -/

/-- A binary combination tree over a carrier type. -/
inductive OpTree (K : Type u) where
  | leaf : K → OpTree K
  | node : OpTree K → OpTree K → OpTree K

namespace OpTree
variable {K : Type u}

/-- Height of a combination tree (longest root-to-leaf path). -/
def height : OpTree K → ℕ
  | leaf _ => 0
  | node l r => max l.height r.height + 1

/-- Number of leaves. -/
def numLeaves : OpTree K → ℕ
  | leaf _ => 1
  | node l r => l.numLeaves + r.numLeaves

/-- Evaluate the tree with a binary operation at every node. -/
def eval (op : K → K → K) : OpTree K → K
  | leaf a => a
  | node l r => op (eval op l) (eval op r)

/-- The maximum `depth` over all leaves. -/
def maxLeafDepth (depth : K → ℕ) : OpTree K → ℕ
  | leaf a => depth a
  | node l r => max (l.maxLeafDepth depth) (r.maxLeafDepth depth)

/-- A complete balanced tree of height `n`, all leaves equal to `a`. -/
def balanced (a : K) : ℕ → OpTree K
  | 0 => leaf a
  | n + 1 => node (balanced a n) (balanced a n)

@[simp] theorem balanced_height (a : K) (n : ℕ) : (balanced a n).height = n := by
  induction n with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ k ih => simp [balanced, height, ih]

@[simp] theorem balanced_maxLeafDepth (depth : K → ℕ) (a : K) (n : ℕ) :
    (balanced a n).maxLeafDepth depth = depth a := by
  induction n with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ k ih => simp [balanced, maxLeafDepth, ih]

@[simp] theorem balanced_numLeaves (a : K) (n : ℕ) : (balanced a n).numLeaves = 2 ^ n := by
  induction n with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ k ih => simp [balanced, numLeaves, ih, pow_succ]; ring

/-- A tree of height `h` has at most `2^h` leaves: height controls size logarithmically. -/
theorem numLeaves_le_pow_height (t : OpTree K) : t.numLeaves ≤ 2 ^ t.height := by
  induction t with
  | leaf a => simp [numLeaves, height]
  | node l r ihl ihr =>
    have hl : l.numLeaves ≤ 2 ^ (max l.height r.height) :=
      le_trans ihl (Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) (le_max_left _ _))
    have hr : r.numLeaves ≤ 2 ^ (max l.height r.height) :=
      le_trans ihr (Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) (le_max_right _ _))
    have hpow : 2 ^ (max l.height r.height + 1) = 2 ^ (max l.height r.height) * 2 := by
      rw [pow_succ]
    simp only [numLeaves, height]
    omega

end OpTree

/-! ### The depth/height bound: depth grows like the height of the combination tree -/

/-- **Logarithmic-overhead theorem (additive).** Evaluating an additive combination tree
    produces depth at most the maximum leaf depth plus the tree height.  The unit-cost
    1-Lipschitz slack accumulates *only along the height*, not the number of leaves.
    Bridge: generalizes `vdepth_triple_sum_bound` to arbitrary combination shapes. -/
theorem depth_eval_add_le (X : DepthCarrier) (t : OpTree X.K) :
    X.depth (t.eval X.add) ≤ t.maxLeafDepth X.depth + t.height := by
  induction t with
  | leaf a => simp [OpTree.eval, OpTree.maxLeafDepth, OpTree.height]
  | node l r ihl ihr =>
    have h := X.depth_add (l.eval X.add) (r.eval X.add)
    simp only [OpTree.eval, OpTree.maxLeafDepth, OpTree.height]
    omega

/-- **Logarithmic-overhead theorem (multiplicative).** Same bound for product trees. -/
theorem depth_eval_mul_le (X : DepthCarrier) (t : OpTree X.K) :
    X.depth (t.eval X.mul) ≤ t.maxLeafDepth X.depth + t.height := by
  induction t with
  | leaf a => simp [OpTree.eval, OpTree.maxLeafDepth, OpTree.height]
  | node l r ihl ihr =>
    have h := X.depth_mul (l.eval X.mul) (r.eval X.mul)
    simp only [OpTree.eval, OpTree.maxLeafDepth, OpTree.height]
    omega

/-- **Balanced corollary (additive).** A balanced additive combination of `2^n` copies of
    a depth-`d` element has depth `≤ d + n`.  Since the tree has `2^n` leaves, the overhead
    is exactly `log₂` of the number of summands — the bridge to `O(log n)` Hensel depth. -/
theorem depth_balanced_eval_le (X : DepthCarrier) (a : X.K) (n : ℕ) :
    X.depth ((OpTree.balanced a n).eval X.add) ≤ X.depth a + n := by
  have h := depth_eval_add_le X (OpTree.balanced a n)
  simpa using h

/-- The balanced corollary, phrased in terms of the leaf count `N = 2^n`. -/
theorem depth_balanced_eval_le_log (X : DepthCarrier) (a : X.K) (n : ℕ) :
    X.depth ((OpTree.balanced a n).eval X.add) ≤ X.depth a + Nat.log 2 ((OpTree.balanced a n).numLeaves) := by
  have h := depth_balanced_eval_le X a n
  have hlog : Nat.log 2 ((OpTree.balanced a n).numLeaves) = n := by
    rw [OpTree.balanced_numLeaves, Nat.log_pow (by norm_num : 1 < 2)]
  rw [hlog]; exact h

/-! ## §5. The Category of Depth Carriers and 1-Lipschitz Morphisms

A morphism of depth carriers preserves the additive structure and is **nonexpansive
(1-Lipschitz) on depth**: `depth (f x) ≤ depth x`.  These morphisms compose, giving a
category that maps functorially into the tropical category. -/

/-- A 1-Lipschitz morphism of depth carriers: preserves `add`, `zero`, and is nonexpansive
    on depth (Lipschitz constant 1). -/
structure DepthHom (X Y : DepthCarrier) where
  toFun : X.K → Y.K
  map_zero' : toFun X.zero = Y.zero
  map_add' : ∀ x y, toFun (X.add x y) = Y.add (toFun x) (toFun y)
  nonexpansive' : ∀ x, Y.depth (toFun x) ≤ X.depth x

instance (X Y : DepthCarrier) : CoeFun (DepthHom X Y) (fun _ => X.K → Y.K) :=
  ⟨DepthHom.toFun⟩

@[ext]
theorem DepthHom.ext {X Y : DepthCarrier} {f g : DepthHom X Y}
    (h : ∀ x, f.toFun x = g.toFun x) : f = g := by
  cases f; cases g; congr; exact funext h

/-- Identity 1-Lipschitz morphism. -/
def DepthHom.id (X : DepthCarrier) : DepthHom X X where
  toFun := _root_.id
  map_zero' := rfl
  map_add' := fun _ _ => rfl
  nonexpansive' := fun _ => le_refl _

/-- Composition of 1-Lipschitz morphisms — nonexpansiveness is preserved by transitivity. -/
def DepthHom.comp {X Y Z : DepthCarrier} (g : DepthHom Y Z) (f : DepthHom X Y) :
    DepthHom X Z where
  toFun x := g.toFun (f.toFun x)
  map_zero' := by rw [f.map_zero', g.map_zero']
  map_add' := fun x y => by rw [f.map_add', g.map_add']
  nonexpansive' := fun x => le_trans (g.nonexpansive' (f.toFun x)) (f.nonexpansive' x)

theorem DepthHom.comp_assoc {W X Y Z : DepthCarrier}
    (h : DepthHom Y Z) (g : DepthHom X Y) (f : DepthHom W X) :
    DepthHom.comp (DepthHom.comp h g) f = DepthHom.comp h (DepthHom.comp g f) := by
  ext x; rfl

theorem DepthHom.comp_id {X Y : DepthCarrier} (f : DepthHom X Y) :
    DepthHom.comp f (DepthHom.id X) = f := by ext x; rfl

theorem DepthHom.id_comp {X Y : DepthCarrier} (f : DepthHom X Y) :
    DepthHom.comp (DepthHom.id Y) f = f := by ext x; rfl

/-- **Composition stays 1-Lipschitz.** The Lipschitz constants multiply: `1 · 1 = 1`. -/
theorem DepthHom.comp_nonexpansive {X Y Z : DepthCarrier}
    (g : DepthHom Y Z) (f : DepthHom X Y) (x : X.K) :
    Z.depth ((DepthHom.comp g f).toFun x) ≤ X.depth x :=
  (DepthHom.comp g f).nonexpansive' x

/-! ## §6. The 1-Lipschitz Functor on Morphisms

`depthTropFunctor` sends each carrier to its tropical depth-value object and each
1-Lipschitz morphism to the identity on `ℕ` (monotone since the order on `ℕ` is reflexive),
exactly mirroring the catalog's `tropicalization_map`.  It is functorial: it preserves
identities and composition. -/

/-- The functor on morphisms: a depth morphism induces the identity tropical morphism on
    the depth-value space `(ℕ, max)`. -/
def depthTropFunctor {X Y : DepthCarrier} (_f : DepthHom X Y) :
    TropHom (depthTropObj X) (depthTropObj Y) where
  toFun := _root_.id
  map_zero' := rfl
  map_one' := rfl
  map_add' := fun _ _ => rfl
  map_mul' := fun _ _ => rfl
  monotone' := fun _ _ h => h

/-- The functor preserves identities. -/
theorem depthTropFunctor_id (X : DepthCarrier) :
    depthTropFunctor (DepthHom.id X) = TropHom.id (depthTropObj X) := by
  ext x; rfl

/-- The functor preserves composition — it is a genuine functor. -/
theorem depthTropFunctor_comp {X Y Z : DepthCarrier}
    (f : DepthHom X Y) (g : DepthHom Y Z) :
    depthTropFunctor (DepthHom.comp g f) =
      TropHom.comp (depthTropFunctor g) (depthTropFunctor f) := by
  ext x; rfl

/-! ## §7. Irreducibility of the unit cost (Lab Note H1, formalized)

The `+1` is genuinely necessary: there is a depth carrier in which doubling strictly
increases depth, so `depth` is *not* a strict tropical valuation (`≤ max`).  This pins
down the novelty — the functor lands in a 1-Lipschitz *relaxation*, never the strict
idempotent tropical world. -/

/-- A witness carrier on `ℕ` whose depth is the identity, with `add = (fun a b => max a b + 1)`.
    Here doubling costs one extra unit, witnessing irreducibility of the unit slack. -/
def witnessCarrier : DepthCarrier where
  K := ℕ
  add := fun a b => max a b + 1
  mul := fun a b => max a b + 1
  zero := 0
  depth := _root_.id
  depth_zero := rfl
  depth_add := fun x y => by simp
  depth_mul := fun x y => by simp

/-- **Irreducibility witness.** In `witnessCarrier`, `depth (add x x) = depth x + 1`,
    so the strict tropical/ultrametric law `depth (add x y) ≤ max (depth x) (depth y)`
    FAILS.  The unit cost cannot be removed. -/
theorem not_strict_ultrametric_witness :
    ∃ (X : DepthCarrier.{0}) (x : X.K),
      ¬ (X.depth (X.add x x) ≤ max (X.depth x) (X.depth x)) := by
  refine ⟨witnessCarrier, (0 : ℕ), ?_⟩
  simp [witnessCarrier]

/-- Evaluating the balanced additive tree of height `n` over `witnessCarrier` (starting from
    `0`) returns exactly `n`: each level adds precisely one unit. -/
theorem balanced_witness_eval (n : ℕ) :
    (OpTree.balanced (0 : ℕ) n).eval witnessCarrier.add = n := by
  induction n with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ k ih =>
    simp only [OpTree.balanced, OpTree.eval]
    rw [ih]
    simp [witnessCarrier]

/-- **Tightness of the logarithmic-overhead bound.** For `witnessCarrier`, the balanced
    bound `depth ≤ depth a + n` of `depth_balanced_eval_le` is attained with EQUALITY:
    the depth of the balanced tree of `2^n` leaves is exactly `depth a + n`.  Hence the
    `log₂`-overhead is not merely an upper bound — it is the true growth rate, and the
    unit Lipschitz cost genuinely accumulates one unit per level. -/
theorem depth_balanced_overhead_tight (n : ℕ) :
    witnessCarrier.depth ((OpTree.balanced (0 : ℕ) n).eval witnessCarrier.add)
      = witnessCarrier.depth (0 : ℕ) + n := by
  rw [balanced_witness_eval]
  simp [witnessCarrier]

/-! ## §8. Compatibility with the catalog's strict reconstruction

Any *strict* depth carrier (one whose depth already satisfies `≤ max`, with no slack, and
which carries the extra negation/multiplicativity data) is a `TropicalValuationCarrier`
in the sense of the catalog, hence reconstructs to a genuine `UltraNormObj`.  We record
the precise gap: strictness is the difference between our 1-Lipschitz functor and the
catalog's exact `valuationReconstruct`. -/

/-- A depth carrier is *strict* if its depth obeys the exact (no-slack) ultrametric law. -/
def IsStrict (X : DepthCarrier) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y, X.depth (X.add x y) ≤ max (X.depth x) (X.depth y)

/-- The standard tropical object `(ℕ, max, ·)` itself, as a strict depth carrier. -/
def tropicalNatCarrier : DepthCarrier where
  K := ℕ
  add := max
  mul := max
  zero := 0
  depth := _root_.id
  depth_zero := rfl
  depth_add := fun x y => by simp
  depth_mul := fun x y => by simp

/-- The standard tropical carrier is strict: `id (max x y) ≤ max x y`. -/
theorem tropicalNatCarrier_isStrict : IsStrict tropicalNatCarrier := by
  intro x y; simp [tropicalNatCarrier]

end ValuationDepthTropicalFunctor

# Future Directions — Korselt's Criterion & the Multiplicative-Order Bridge

Derived from the research cycle that produced
`Catalog/Shared/KorseltCriterion.lean` (the full Korselt **iff** and its
arbitrary-exponent generalization) and
`Catalog/Cryptography/KorseltGroupActionBridge.lean` (the order/exponent-collapse
bridge into group actions).

This cycle proved, unconditionally:

* **C1** — Korselt's criterion is an iff: for `n > 1`,
  `IsAbsFermatPsp n ↔ IsKorselt n` (`korselt_iff_absFermatPsp`), with the hard
  squarefree converse `squarefree_of_forall_units_pow_one` via Cauchy on
  `(ℤ/p²ℤ)ˣ`.
* **C2** — Generalized Korselt: for squarefree `n` and *any* exponent `e`,
  `(∀ u : (ℤ/nℤ)ˣ, u ^ e = 1) ↔ ∀ p ∣ n prime, (p − 1) ∣ e`
  (`generalized_korselt`, `generalized_korselt_modEq`).
* **C4/C5** — Order/exponent collapse: `Monoid.exponent (ℤ/nℤ)ˣ ∣ (n − 1)` and
  `≤ n − 1` for Korselt `n` (`korselt_exponent_dvd`, `korselt_exponent_le`); the
  "exponentiate-by-`n−1`" map is the identity on every torsor, with an iff for the
  regular action (`korselt_iff_regular_pow_trivial`).

The analysis below lists the next falsifiable steps.

## D1 — The Carmichael lambda is exactly the per-prime lcm

**Conjecture.** For squarefree `n`,
`Monoid.exponent (ℤ/nℤ)ˣ = Nat.lcm’ {p − 1 : p prime, p ∣ n}` (the Carmichael
function `λ(n)`), and `IsKorselt n ↔ λ(n) ∣ (n − 1)`.

**The key insight is** that `generalized_korselt` already characterizes the set of
*all* exponents `e` killing every unit as exactly `{e : ∀ p ∣ n, (p−1) ∣ e}`; the
monoid exponent is the least positive such `e`, which is by definition the lcm of
the `p − 1`.

**Why now?** Both inequalities are within reach: `forall_units_pow_one_of_korselt`
gives `λ ∣ lcm`, and `prime_sub_one_dvd_of_forall_units_pow_one` applied to
`e := Monoid.exponent` gives `(p−1) ∣ λ`, hence `lcm ∣ λ`.

## D2 — Korselt numbers have at least three prime factors

**Conjecture.** Every Korselt (Carmichael) number is a product of at least three
distinct odd primes; in particular no Korselt number is even and none is a product
of two primes.

**The key insight is** that `korselt_orderOf_dvd` forces `(p − 1) ∣ (n − 1)` for
each prime factor while `p ∣ n` forces `p ∤ (n − 1)`; combining these parity/size
constraints across few prime factors yields a contradiction (the classical
Korselt count argument), now phrased over the order spectrum of `∏ (ℤ/pℤ)ˣ`.

**Why now?** The squarefree converse and `(p − 1) ∣ (n − 1)` are both established,
so the only missing ingredient is a finite case analysis on the number of prime
factors — pure `omega`/`Nat` arithmetic on the proven divisibilities.

## D3 — Order-collapse density and a single-witness Fermat test

**Conjecture.** For a Korselt `n` with `k` distinct prime factors, the fraction of
units `a` with `orderOf a` a *proper* divisor of `n − 1` is at least
`1 − 2^{-(k−1)}`, so one random base detects the collapse with bounded-away-from-0
probability.

**The key insight is** that `korselt_orderOf_dvd` makes *every* order divide
`n − 1`; via the CRT isomorphism `(ℤ/nℤ)ˣ ≃ ∏ (ℤ/pℤ)ˣ` the proportion of bases
realizing the *full* exponent is a product of cyclic-group counting fractions,
each `≤ 1/2` for the 2-adic obstruction.

**Why now?** The order-divisibility fact is now a first-class lemma; turning it
into a density bound needs only `Fintype.card` arithmetic over the CRT product, no
new number theory.

## D4 — Free actions cannot hide a hard GAIP on a Korselt modulus

**Conjecture.** No free `MulAction` of `(ℤ/nℤ)ˣ` on a torsor `X` (with `n`
Korselt) admits a group-action inverse problem harder than `O(√(n−1))`: the
universal relation collapses the effective key space to `λ(n) ∣ (n − 1)`, enabling
baby-step/giant-step.

**The key insight is** that `korselt_action_pow_trivial` plus `free_smul_iff` show
the connector group element is constrained to a subgroup of exponent `λ(n)`, so the
search space has size `λ(n) ≤ n − 1`, and `korselt_exponent_le` makes the
`√` baby-step/giant-step bound explicit.

**Why now?** `korselt_exponent_le` and the geometric-triviality lemmas already live
on the exact `MulAction` interface; quantifying the BSGS cost is the next theorem.

## D5 — Strong-pseudoprime refinement via the 2-adic valuation

**Conjecture.** A Korselt `n` survives the strong (Miller–Rabin) test for base `a`
iff the 2-adic valuation `v₂(orderOf a)` matches a common value across all prime
factors; the density of strong liars is governed by `min_p v₂(p − 1)`.

**The key insight is** that the generalized exponent framework isolates the
contribution of each `p − 1`; splitting `n − 1 = 2^s · t` and tracking
`v₂(p − 1)` per prime turns the strong-pseudoprime condition into a per-factor
2-Sylow alignment, refining the plain order collapse of D3.

**Why now?** `generalized_korselt` already decomposes the exponent condition
prime-by-prime, so restricting attention to the 2-part is a direct specialization
rather than a new decomposition.
